claims.hypothesis: The emission lines near 232 GHz toward Betelgeuse are Rydberg transition lines (H30alpha and an X30alpha blend of heavier elements)
claims.experiment: Compared observed line frequencies with Rydberg-formula rest frequencies, ruled out TiO2, and computed model line profiles from a semi-empirical atmosphere
claims.result: Observed lines lie near the H30alpha and X30alpha cluster frequencies and the model reproduces the X30alpha emission on and off the disk
claims.finding: The lines are identified as H30alpha and X30alpha

evidence.quote: These simulations confirm the identity of the Rydberg transition lines observed towards Betelgeuse

claims.hypothesis: Line wings are better described by Voigt than Gaussian profiles, with electron collisional broadening contributing
claims.experiment: Fitted Voigt and Gaussian profiles to integrated spectra and applied a collisional broadening approximation to the H30alpha Lorentzian
claims.result: Voigt fits are better; the Lorentzian component implies ne of about 3e8 cm^-3
claims.finding: Electron densities in the hotter chromosphere are consistent with collisional broadening

evidence.quote: Line shapes show wings consistent with Voigt rather than Gaussian profiles
Because of the strong dependence on the Rydberg transition, measurements of the widths of other lines would be of interest to confirm this mechanism.

limitations_admitted.value: Model is a mean 1D lukewarm chromosphere, without hot small-filling-factor plasma or cold molecular pockets

evidence.quote: This model represents the mean 1D dominant lukewarm chromosphere and not the small filling factor of hot chromospheric plasma that gives rise to the rich UV spectrum.
It also does not include pockets of cold molecular material.
